outcome: incidence of survival without major morbidities
cohort: Preterm infants born to mothers with SLE (exposed group) and a matched control group of preterm infants born to mothers without SLE, all from Shanghai Children's Medical Center between 2012 and 2021.
finding: Born to mothers with SLE may not increase the risk of major premature morbidities, but it is associated with differences in the hematologic profile of preterm infants, and maternal aspirin administration was associated with a reduced risk of very preterm birth and increased survival without major morbidities among SLE preterm infants.
